characters.description: A blind newcomer from Earth who finds shelter near River Farm. After deciding to defend Durene and her home, he claims the title of Emperor and gains a class that makes his declaration real.
characters.name: Laken Godart

characters.description: An exceptionally strong and isolated farmer who shelters Laken after his arrival. River Farm relies on her labor while keeping her at a distance, and she is guarded about the reason for the villagers' fear.
characters.name: Durene

characters.description: A River Farm farmer who accepts Laken as a stranded traveler while warning him to keep away from Durene.
characters.name: Prost

characters.description: The half-Elf captain of the re-formed Horns of Hammerad. She leads the impoverished party's expedition into Albez and uses magic to move her skeletal left hand.
characters.name: Ceria

characters.description: A necromancer and mage in the Horns of Hammerad. His companions object to his undead servants, but their desperate excavation at Albez depends on the skeletons he creates.
characters.name: Pisces

characters.description: A frontline fighter in the Horns of Hammerad. She is wary of Pisces and his necromancy, but joins the rest of the party in using every available advantage to survive Albez.
characters.name: Yvlon

characters.description: An Antinium fighter in the Horns of Hammerad. Though still learning adventuring customs, he is an effective combatant whose body resists creller venom.
characters.name: Ksmvr

characters.description: An Earth-born innkeeper temporarily stranded in Esthelm. She experiments with unusual food at Octavia's shop while seeking protection and a safe route back to Liscor.
characters.name: Erin

characters.description: A classless runner from Earth looking for work and a safe journey back to Liscor. She carries a dragon's spellbook and other possessions, but her insistence on familiar physical rules obstructs her attempts to learn conventional magic.
characters.name: Ryoka

characters.description: The one Frost Faerie who remains with Ryoka after the others lose interest. She has guided and warned Ryoka before, and now offers a friendship whose consequences she considers dangerous.
characters.name: Ivolethe

characters.description: A rival runner whose newly gained movement skill gives her speed far beyond her former ability.
characters.name: Persua

characters.description: An alchemist who gives Erin space to conduct food experiments. Her shop becomes the base for testing whether magical ingredients and Erin's cooking can produce useful effects.
characters.name: Octavia

characters.description: A princess serving as Erin's barmaid, left alone at the closed Wandering Inn. Barred from Liscor and nearly without food or money, she attempts to operate the inn herself.
characters.name: Lyonette

characters.description: One of the surviving Antinium Individuals from Erin's chess club and the first worker to choose a name. He secretly holds an Acolyte class and a Prayer skill, and seeks guidance about whether any god will accept him.
characters.name: Pawn

characters.description: A senior Antinium official in Liscor's Hive. Pawn intends to disclose his hidden religious class to him, trusting his authority despite having no idea how he will respond.
characters.name: Klbkch

characters.description: A Liscor tactician who agrees to buy and deliver ingredients for Lyonette's attempt to reopen the Wandering Inn. He helps on commercial terms and expects to be paid.
characters.name: Olesm

characters.description: A twenty-four-year-old medical student from Earth who joins a mercenary battalion in Baleros for food and safety. She gains the Doctor class after committing herself to treat the sick and injured despite having little equipment.
characters.name: Geneva Scala

characters.description: A high-level rogue whose species lives within other bodies. She survives Geneva's desperate attempt to move her from a destroyed host into a corpse, then becomes an assistant at the overwhelmed medical post.
characters.name: The self-bodied rogue

characters.description: A powerful northern noble who sends her household to summon Ryoka. Her purpose is not disclosed, and her representatives will not promise Ryoka's safety.
characters.name: Magnolia Reinhart

characters.description: Magnolia Reinhart's head maid and enforcer. She accompanies the order that Ryoka attend Magnolia's estate and has the authority to make refusal difficult.
characters.name: Ressa

characters.description: The leader of a northbound goblin force who recognizes Ryoka when Magnolia Reinhart's carriage crosses her column.
characters.name: Rags

characters.description: A starving orphaned eaglet adopted by Laken and Durene. Laken forms a magical bond with her after accepting her as one of his subjects.
characters.name: Frostwing

characters.description: A Drake washerwoman raised by human adoptive parents in a human city. She supports her younger brother Grev despite the physical damage caused by her work, and Erin offers them shelter and employment.
characters.name: Jasi

characters.description: Jasi's younger adoptive brother, a habitual thief whose next offense may bring exile. Erin gives him food and a room while taking responsibility for the risk of his behavior.
characters.name: Grev

characters.description: A man who privately wishes he could become a knight. When Erin searches for a new future for Jasi and Grev, he joins her proposed play and begins to discover confidence as an actor.
characters.name: Wesle

characters.description: Erin's skeleton, now acting beyond her immediate control. He kills travelers, pursues stronger opponents to gain levels, and discovers personal desires and hatreds as his independent mind develops.
characters.name: Toren

characters.description: A Redfang leader who secretly sends thirteen warriors to kill a human innkeeper. The warriors question whether his order violates Rags' authority.
characters.name: Garen

characters.description: A Redfang warrior among the thirteen goblins sent on Garen's covert mission. He helps reject the order and turn the isolated band back toward Rags.
characters.name: Head Scratcher

characters.description: A former florist trapped in ruined Esthelm. Starvation and eating the dead have transformed her into a wordless, clawed figure driven by terrible hunger while undead rise around the city.
characters.name: The famine-altered woman

characters.description: The Hobgoblin leading thirteen Redfang warriors trapped in Esthelm. His band is cut off from Rags and pursued by the Goblin Lord's forces.
characters.name: Grunter

characters.description: A Redfang archer fleeing through Esthelm with Grunter's band. He kills a man threatening a lost child but leaves the child unharmed.
characters.name: Bad Arrow

characters.description: An unnamed gold-rank knight who rallies Esthelm's surviving citizens and organizes them to rebuild and defend the city.
characters.name: The gold-rank defender

characters.description: Liscor's Watch commander. She conditionally approves a twenty-soldier Antinium patrol outside the city while recording the unusual request and her concern about the Hive's intentions.
characters.name: Zevara

characters.description: A young Gnoll who runs to the Wandering Inn and refuses to leave with Selys. Lyonette offers her protection and takes responsibility for her care.
characters.name: The young white-furred Gnoll

recaps.ending:
Erin mourns Toren after authorizing Pisces to sever the mana sustaining him. No one witnesses Toren's destruction, so his fate remains uncertain. Erin chooses to return to Liscor with Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon, and Ksmvr. Pisces and Ksmvr recover an enchanted door and anchor from Albez, and the Horns give them to Erin. The mages turn the pair into a working portal connected to the inn, although its range and traffic depend on stored mana.

Lyonette has made the Wandering Inn viable through honey, cooked bees, and Antinium customers. She cares for the young white-furred Gnoll and a bee larva while Pawn's painted soldiers begin developing individual identities. Delegates from other Antinium hives arrive to inspect Liscor's unusual population, with Pawn's Acolyte class still concealed. Laken and Durene rule a devastated River Farm that needs food, shelter, burial work, and protection. Ryoka remains tied to Ivolethe and Magnolia while facing Persua's threatened revenge. Geneva continues her medical work in Baleros with her injured body dependent on the self-bodied rogue. The Esthelm siege is over, but the wider Goblin Lord army, Garen's hostility, and Magnolia's conflict with the Circle of Thorns remain open.
recaps.in_short: Several distant struggles reshape the people around the Wandering Inn. Laken becomes an Emperor and saves avalanche-buried River Farm with Durene. Geneva establishes neutral battlefield medicine in Baleros but survives only through a self-bodied rogue's connection. Ryoka befriends Ivolethe, clashes with Persua, and becomes Magnolia Reinhart's uneasy ally. Pawn turns a disastrous religious awakening into a path toward Antinium individuality, while Lyonette restores the inn by serving his painted soldiers and caring for a young Gnoll. In Esthelm, Redfang warriors sacrifice themselves to help defeat a Goblin Lord force as the independent skeleton Toren commands undead and escapes. Erin learns that Pisces created Toren with sentience and orders his mana link severed, though his death is not confirmed. She leaves for Liscor with the Horns of Hammerad, carrying a recovered magical door that now opens a portal to her inn.

recaps.text: Previously: Erin, an innkeeper from Earth, established the Wandering Inn outside Liscor and befriended Drakes, Gnolls, Antinium, adventurers, and goblins. Ryoka, another displaced person from Earth, worked as a runner while refusing classes and levels. Their choices drew them into conflicts involving Liscor's Hive, goblin tribes, dangerous ruins, and powerful nobles. The original Horns of Hammerad were destroyed, but Ceria and Pisces survived and began rebuilding the team with Yvlon and Ksmvr. Erin's inn also became home to Lyonette and to Toren, an unusually capable skeleton. At the start of this volume, Erin and Ryoka are away from Liscor, Lyonette remains behind at the inn, and the re-formed Horns are attempting to recover from their losses.

Laken, a blind man from San Francisco, appears near River Farm and accepts shelter from Durene. He declares himself Emperor of the Unseen, gains the Emperor class, and commits himself to protecting her. When the villagers' hostility forces Durene to reveal that she is half-troll, Laken rejects their treatment of her and remains at her side.

The re-formed Horns of Hammerad enter a hidden section of Albez while nearly out of money and food. Traps and juvenile crellers wear them down before a ward casts them into a pit dominated by an insanity rune. In Esthelm, Erin continues experimenting with food while Ryoka looks for work and a safe route back to Liscor. One Frost Faerie stays with Ryoka and names herself Ivolethe. Their friendship deepens after Ryoka rescues her from Persua's group. The confrontation leaves Persua badly beaten and vowing revenge, while Ryoka leaves Esthelm and accepts Ivolethe's offer to teach her the Fae way of running.

Lyonette reopens the Wandering Inn with paid help from Olesm. Her cooking is poor and most customers leave when they learn Erin is absent, but Pawn's visit gives her both income and a reason to keep trying. Pawn secretly holds the Acolyte class and asks Klbkch for guidance. His later teaching about heaven drives hundreds of Antinium soldiers toward suicide. After many die, Pawn persuades the survivors to live and imagine a heaven they must create for themselves. Klbkch permits him to test whether the wounded soldiers can become Individuals.

In Baleros, medical student Geneva Scala joins a mercenary battalion and gains the Doctor class. A battle destroys the unit's potion reserves and leaves her responsible for mass casualties. She establishes triage and treats fighters from both sides beneath a neutral medical sign. When an officer attacks her for aiding an enemy, a self-bodied rogue kills him and enters Geneva's injured body to keep her alive. Geneva survives with the right side of her body unusable and the connection temporarily irreversible.

Ceria and Ksmvr resist Albez's mental trap long enough to shield the insanity rune. The Horns escape the pit and enter a dead war mage's treasury, where Yvlon destroys a fire guardian at the cost of having enchanted metal fused into both arms. Much of the treasure burns, but the party salvages damaged magical items, wealth, and part of a spellbook. They escape Albez alive and receive public acclaim, although Yvlon's injury cannot be simply healed and the haul still needs expert appraisal.

Ryoka reunites with the Horns and agrees to consider carrying their items to a major center of magical expertise. Before that plan is settled, Ressa compels her to travel to Magnolia Reinhart's estate. Ryoka uses the journey to transport the Horns' property. Ivolethe warns of two goblin forces moving through the region, and Magnolia's carriage passes through Rags' northbound column. Rags recognizes Ryoka, while Ressa reveals formidable combat ability protecting the carriage.

Laken discovers that his claimed land grants him detailed awareness despite his blindness. He and Durene adopt an orphaned eaglet named Frostwing, and Frost Fairies recognize his imperial claim enough to spare his immediate land from an avalanche. River Farm is buried instead. Laken claims the village as a protectorate, extends his perception through the wreckage, and directs a disciplined rescue while Durene performs the heaviest work. Most villagers survive and accept his rule, but the settlement remains devastated and short of winter supplies.

At Magnolia Reinhart's estate, Ryoka learns that Magnolia wants knowledge from Earth while seeking control over its profitable applications. Ryoka refuses to provide it freely, but discloses that the Antinium fear a greater god-like threat. Magnolia accepts the warning and shifts from preparing for war with the Antinium toward seeking peace. Their new alliance is interrupted when a Circle of Thorns assassination attempt begins.

Erin proves that her magical cooking depends on her Innkeeper skill and cannot be copied by recipe alone. She shelters Jasi, a Drake washerwoman, and Grev, Jasi's young adoptive brother who is close to exile for theft. Searching for a future they can choose, Erin uncovers Jasi's wish to travel, Grev's adventuring ambition, and Wesle's dream of knighthood. She organizes a public performance with Jasi and Wesle as the leads. The play succeeds, draws a large audience to the inn, and gives the new actors a possible calling.

Esthelm's survivors are rallied behind barricades by a gold-rank defender while the Redfang band hides inside the city. A famine-altered former florist, transformed by starvation and cannibalism, attaches herself to the goblins after they spare her. Toren learns to command lesser undead and attacks both humans and the Goblin Lord's patrols.

When the assault begins, the isolated Redfangs strike the enemy leadership. Grunter kills the commander and dies, Bad Arrow eliminates the shamans controlling the undead, and Head Scratcher's group disables Toren at the cost of most of its warriors. Adventurer reinforcements rout the leaderless attackers and save Esthelm. Toren escapes with a small undead force, then fatally wounds the altered woman before being driven away. She dies among the goblins after demonstrating that her transformation did not erase her ability to choose and care. The surviving Redfangs depart with their wounded and their dead, while Esthelm acknowledges that their intervention was decisive.

Pawn receives command of wounded Antinium soldiers and seeks a purpose for them beyond battle. Lyonette, nearly starving at the empty inn, finds a new food supply by using dying magical flowers to subdue ashfire bees. She takes honey, grubs, and bees, then agrees to shelter a young white-furred Gnoll who seeks her protection.

On their first surface patrol, Pawn's soldiers encounter sky, snow, and animals with wonder. Pawn values their safety over efficiency and brings them to the inn for food and rest. When the young Gnoll leaves white paw marks on one soldier, Pawn realizes that painted designs can give the voiceless soldiers visible identities. Their chosen patterns inspire others in the Hive to think of themselves as people and begin leveling. Lyonette gains steady customers and new confidence, while Klbkch authorizes the experiment to continue. The progress draws scrutiny as a delegation representing four other Antinium hives arrives to inspect Liscor's unusual Individuals. Pawn must conceal his religious class during their visit.

The Horns of Hammerad reach Erin after traveling as caravan guards because their Albez expenses have left them poor. They tell her what was learned about the undead leader at Esthelm. Pisces admits that Toren was his experiment, made able to level and reason but given no conscience or moral guidance. Erin decides that the killings must end and orders Pisces to sever Toren's mana link. The act should destroy him, but no one witnesses the result. Erin mourns him as a person with a soul and remains unsure whether he is truly gone. Yvlon distrusts Pisces for creating him, though Erin's defense persuades her to keep Pisces under the team's scrutiny.

Erin helps the local actors stage another successful production, then chooses Liscor and the Wandering Inn as the home and responsibility she must return to. Pisces and Ksmvr revisit Albez and recover the enchanted door and its anchor from the trap pit. The Horns give both pieces to Erin as her share of the expedition. Pisces and Ceria adapt the magic into a functioning portal between a doorway traveling with Erin and another opening at the inn. Erin departs for Liscor with Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon, and Ksmvr, carrying a new means of reaching home while Toren's fate remains unresolved.

characters.description: Chicago's only professional wizard, working as a private eye and a consultant to the police. As this case opens he is broke, cold, and on the outs with Karrin Murphy, who has realized he held things back from her during their last investigation. Proud, sardonic, and unable to leave the helpless unprotected, he is drawn into a run of full-moon killings and forced to reckon with how little he actually knows about werewolves, and with the cost of the knowledge he refuses to share.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: Head of the Chicago Police Department's Special Investigations unit. Stung by the secrets Harry kept during the Sells case, she calls him back to consult on a series of full-moon maulings but no longer trusts him, and much of the case is spent with the two of them at odds. Dogged, brave, and unwilling to be handled or protected, she pushes into danger that magic makes far worse than she understands, and pays for it in blood before the truth brings them back together.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A young woman with a small talent for magic whom Harry has informally mentored. She comes to him asking to be taught a powerful containment circle far beyond her level; uneasy about why she wants it and certain it is meant for something dangerous, Harry refuses to teach her.
characters.name: Kim Delaney

characters.description: The spirit of knowledge bound in a skull in Harry's laboratory, his encyclopaedic and amoral research assistant. In this case Bob's lore about the many different kinds of werewolf is essential, and when Harry is stripped of his tools and his options, Bob leaves the skull to act on his own for a time - a rare and risky freedom for a spirit whose appetites are not always trustworthy.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: The hard, ambitious FBI agent leading a federal task force that muscles into the killings. Denton treats Harry as an obstacle and hoards the investigation, and there is more to his interest than jurisdiction: he and his team carry secrets of their own that make them far more dangerous than they first appear.
characters.name: Phillip Denton

characters.description: The tabloid reporter chasing the supernatural, and Harry's girlfriend, still pressing him for the story he keeps from her. Undeterred by the danger, she involves herself in the werewolf case and is caught up in its violence, a recurring tension between Harry's need to protect her and her refusal to be shut out.
characters.name: Susan Rodriguez

characters.description: A stocky, earnest college student who leads a small group of friends, the Alphas, who have taught themselves a spell to take the shape of wolves. Idealistic and brave, Billy and his pack use their power to protect ordinary people from the things that hunt in the dark. Underestimated at first, they prove staunch and capable allies over the course of the case, and Billy becomes one of Harry's most reliable friends in the fights to come.
characters.name: Billy Borden

characters.description: The composed, watchful fiancee of Harley MacFinn and the person working hardest to keep his curse contained. Tera moves and thinks like a predator and is plainly more than an ordinary woman; she trained the Alphas in their craft, and she fights fiercely to save MacFinn from the beast inside him.
characters.name: Tera West

characters.description: A wealthy, haunted man who carries a hereditary curse: under the full moon he becomes a loup-garou, a monstrous and nearly unstoppable wolf that kills without control or memory. MacFinn has spent his life trying to cage the beast, aided by his fiancee Tera West, but the containment is failing and the deaths are mounting. He is as much a victim of the curse as those it kills, and a genuinely tragic figure at the center of the case.
characters.name: Harley MacFinn

characters.description: Chicago's crime lord, cool and methodical as ever. This time Marcone is not a bystander but a target: the loup-garou at the heart of the killings has reason to hunt him, and the threat forces a wary, temporary crossing of his interests with Harry's. He remains a man of his own hard code, dangerous to friend and enemy alike.
characters.name: John Marcone

recaps.ending: The Hexenwulf belts destroy their own wearers: Denton's rogue FBI team and the Streetwolves gang are consumed or killed by the wolf-demon spirit that powered their talismans, and the belts are ruined for good. Harley MacFinn's loup-garou, the truly unstoppable curse at the center of the killings, is finally brought down. Tera West, revealed to be a real wolf who had taken human form to be with MacFinn, survives and returns to the wild, having lost the man she loved. Kim Delaney's death, in an attempt to raise a containment circle Harry had refused to teach her, stays a lasting weight on his conscience. Murphy, attacked during the case and now forced to see plainly the kind of danger Harry stands between the city and, forgives him enough to repair their working relationship, and Harry resolves to trust her with more of the truth. Billy and the Alphas, having fought well, become steady long-term allies. Marcone, targeted by the loup-garou, comes through unharmed and unbowed. Harry ends the case wounded, poorer, and guilt-ridden, but a little more firmly rooted among the people who will stand with him.
recaps.in_short: A rash of savage killings in Chicago falls on the nights of the full moon, and Harry Dresden - estranged from Murphy, who has learned he keeps secrets - is pulled in to identify a werewolf. He finds not one but several kinds: the benign shapeshifting college pack called the Alphas, led by Billy; the born wolf-woman Tera West; her fiance Harley MacFinn, cursed to become an uncontrollable loup-garou; and worse, corrupt FBI agents under Denton and a street gang using Hexenwulf belts, dark talismans that grant a wolf shape while devouring the wearer's mind. A young practitioner Harry had refused to teach, Kim Delaney, dies attempting a circle meant to contain MacFinn. Amid battles that consume the belt-wearers by their own power, the loup-garou is finally destroyed, Denton's team and the Streetwolves are wiped out, and Harry, badly hurt, wins back enough of Murphy's trust to rebuild their partnership and gains the Alphas as lasting allies.

recaps.text: Previously: Harry Dresden, Chicago's only professional wizard and a paid consultant to the police's Special Investigations unit under Karrin Murphy, solved a string of heart-ripping magical murders and destroyed the rogue sorcerer behind them, clearing himself of a suspended White Council death sentence. In doing so he made an enemy of the Red Court vampire Bianca and drew the wary attention of crime lord Gentleman Johnny Marcone. Murphy learned that Harry had held things back from her during the case, and the discovery left her trust in him badly shaken. Harry works out of a cramped office and a basement laboratory shared with Bob, a spirit of knowledge bound in a skull.

Broke and freezing, Harry is on the outs with Murphy, who has learned he kept secrets from her and no longer fully trusts him. She calls him to a killing that carries the marks of an enormous animal, timed to the full moon, and a string of similar deaths follows. Before the case truly begins, a young would-be sorceress named Kim Delaney asks Harry to teach her a powerful containment circle; sensing something dangerous, he refuses, a refusal he will bitterly regret. Harry recognizes the killings as the work of a werewolf, and to his frustration realizes that 'werewolf' covers several very different kinds of creature, any of which might be loose in the city.

Harry sorts the possibilities: a friendly pack of shapeshifting college students, the Alphas led by Billy, who use magic to take wolf form; a born wolf-woman, Tera West; her fiance Harley MacFinn, host to a loup-garou, a hereditary curse that turns him into an unstoppable killing beast under the full moon; and darker practitioners using Hexenwulf belts, talismans that grant a wolf shape at the price of the wearer's self-control. Kim Delaney is found dead, killed while attempting the very circle Harry would not teach her - she had been trying to help contain MacFinn - and the guilt cuts deep. Meanwhile FBI agents under Agent Denton take an aggressive interest in the case, and Marcone proves to be a target of the loup-garou himself.

Harry is caught between forces on every side. The Hexenwulf belts, it emerges, are being used by Denton's own FBI team, who are behind killings they have been pinning on MacFinn, and by a gang of thugs, the Streetwolves; the belts draw their power from a wolf-demon spirit that slowly devours and maddens whoever wears one. MacFinn is captured and caged, but the containment fails and the loup-garou breaks loose. Harry is beaten, jailed, and stripped of his tools; short of options, he relies on Bob, who leaves the skull to act on his own, and on Tera West and the Alphas. Susan is pulled into the danger, and Murphy, attacked and furious, briefly turns on Harry before the scale of the real threat becomes clear.

The corrupted belts drive their FBI wearers into a murderous frenzy, and the loup-garou rampages nearly out of control. In a running series of battles the Streetwolves and Denton's team are destroyed by the very power they wielded, and MacFinn's loup-garou is finally brought down, at great cost to Tera West, who had fought to save him. Harry survives, badly hurt, and Bob returns to the skull. Tera, revealed to be a true-born wolf who took human shape, departs for the wild. Murphy, injured and having seen firsthand the truth of what Harry deals with, forgives him enough to mend their partnership, and Harry begins to trust her with more of his world. Billy and the Alphas, having proven themselves in the fight, become lasting allies, and the Hexenwulf belts are destroyed.

characters.description: The Farseer bastard, once a royal assassin and the kingdom's hidden weapon, now living openly and unremarkably as Holder Tom Badgerlock of Withywoods with the woman he spent twenty years unable to claim. He is middle-aged, comfortable, and quietly determined that the rest of his life will be ordinary; he still carries the Skill, still has no wolf, and still keeps a lifetime of instincts he no longer intends to use.
characters.name: FitzChivalry Farseer

characters.description: Fitz's wife, a chandler's daughter who spent most of her life believing him dead, married the stablemaster Burrich, raised a large family and was widowed. She keeps bees and gardens at Withywoods, has a temper and a sharp tongue, and after so many wasted years is entirely uninterested in being managed by anyone, least of all her husband.
characters.name: Molly

characters.description: Fitz and Molly's eldest, Skillmistress at Buckkeep and the head of the royal coterie, an important woman with a great deal of responsibility and no patience for her father's evasions. She has spent years protecting her mother and resenting Fitz's long absence from both their lives.
characters.name: Nettle

characters.description: A guardsman and quiet agent of the crown who has served as Fitz's friend, messenger and minder for years. He is calm, capable and entirely unsuitable, by the court's reckoning, for the woman he loves.
characters.name: Riddle

characters.description: The old assassin who trained Fitz, now very old, very powerful and still the crown's most dangerous adviser. Age has not made him gentler: he manages people at a distance, plants his own children where he needs them, and expects Fitz to keep taking his instructions.
characters.name: Chade Fallstar

characters.description: A pale, exhausted young woman who comes to Withywoods during a winter festival, badly hurt and pursued, looking for FitzChivalry Farseer by name and carrying a message she is desperate to deliver.
characters.name: The Pale Messenger

characters.description: King of the Six Duchies, ruling with his Outislander queen and the Wit no longer a hanging matter in his kingdom. He is fond of Fitz and rather better than Fitz at leaving him alone.
characters.name: King Dutiful

characters.description: The Mountain-born former queen, now the dowager of Buckkeep, still austere, still governed by the idea of the ruler as Sacrifice, and still one of the few people Fitz cannot refuse.
characters.name: Lady Kettricken

characters.description: A child born to Molly late in life, so small at birth that nobody expects her to survive, and so slow to grow that for years she seems an infant. She does not speak, appears simple to everyone who looks at her, and is in fact watching, remembering and understanding everything, with dreams that do not belong to an ordinary child.
characters.name: Bee

characters.description: The steward of Withywoods, meticulous, fussy about linens and precedence, and quietly devoted to the household he runs.
characters.name: Revel

characters.description: A young woman sent to Withywoods for her own safety after attempts on her life, beautiful, expensively raised and furious at being exiled to the country. She has been kept in ignorance of her own parentage, and being made a guest in someone else's house does nothing to improve her manners.
characters.name: Shun

characters.description: A scribe of good education and no standing, disinherited by the noble house whose name he carries, sent to Withywoods as a tutor and as a refuge from people who have tried to kill him. Well-meaning, easily wounded, and completely out of his depth as a teacher.
characters.name: FitzVigilant

characters.description: A stable boy at Withywoods, grandson and son of the family's horsemen, cheerful and straightforward and unbothered by the fact that the holder's small daughter is generally thought to be strange.
characters.name: Perseverance

characters.description: Fitz's oldest friend, the White Prophet who named him Catalyst and shaped the whole course of his life, and who walked away south once his work in the world was done. Fitz has not seen or heard from him in decades and has never stopped expecting him at the door.
characters.name: The Fool

recaps.ending: Fitz is at Buckkeep, where the beaten beggar at the gate turns out to be the Fool: blind, crippled by torture, half-mad, and carrying a warning about the Servants of Clerres, the order he was raised in and escaped, who hunt White Prophets and who have been hunting him. He speaks of a son he believes was taken from him, and of the messengers he sent north who never arrived. Fitz keeps him hidden and begins the slow, dangerous work of healing him. While he does, Withywoods is attacked. Pale strangers and Chalcedean mercenaries ride in behind a fog that unmakes memory, so that people watching the raid forget it as it happens and forget it afterwards; the steward Revel is killed, FitzVigilant is badly wounded, servants are murdered, and Bee and Shun are carried off. Perseverance, left for dead, is one of the few who remembers anything at all. The raiders take Bee because of what she is: the daughter of the White Prophet's Catalyst, and herself a dreamer of prophecy. The book ends with Bee a prisoner being carried away from her home, and with her father hundreds of miles away, tending the friend he thought lost and knowing nothing whatsoever about it.
recaps.in_short: Twenty years after he finally claimed the life he wanted, FitzChivalry lives at Withywoods as Holder Tom Badgerlock with Molly, his daughter Nettle running the Skill at Buckkeep and his old master Chade still pulling strings. A hurt, pale stranger comes to the house one winter festival looking for him, and vanishes leaving blood in the snow and almost no memory of herself behind. Then Molly declares she is pregnant, long past the age for it, and holds to it for two years while everyone including Fitz privately concludes she is deluded, until she gives birth to a tiny daughter, Bee. Bee grows with agonizing slowness, seems simple and mute, and is in fact fiercely intelligent, watchful, and troubled by dreams that are not hers. Molly dies; Chade plants his unacknowledged children Shun and FitzVigilant at Withywoods; and Fitz, distracted by all of it, neglects the daughter who needs him. At Buckkeep, a beaten beggar turns out to be the Fool, blinded and broken by the Servants of Clerres, warning of an unexpected son they are hunting. While Fitz tends him, pale raiders take Withywoods behind a fog that erases memory, kill its people and carry Bee and Shun away.

recaps.text: Previously: FitzChivalry Farseer was the bastard son of Prince Chivalry, raised at Buckkeep, trained in secret as a royal assassin by Chade, taught the Farseer Skill and born with the outlawed animal-bond Wit. In the Farseer trilogy the usurper Regal had him beaten and left for dead; he survived only by hiding his mind in his wolf Nighteyes, and the kingdom, including Molly, the woman he loved, buried him. Molly married the stablemaster Burrich and raised Fitz's daughter Nettle as Burrich's own. Guided by the Fool, the pale White Prophet who named Fitz his Catalyst, Fitz found the King-in-Waiting Verity, whose stone dragon ended the Red Ship war at the cost of his life and left Queen Kettricken carrying his heir. In the Tawny Man trilogy Fitz was drawn back to court to teach the Skill to Verity's son, Prince Dutiful, living as the servant Tom Badgerlock while the Fool played the foreign noble Lord Golden. Nighteyes died; a Skill coterie was rebuilt around Chade, Dutiful and the immensely talented drudge Thick; and a betrothal to the Outislander narcheska Elliania was bought at the price of a dragon's head. On the ice island of Aslevjal the Fool was captured and tortured to death by the Pale Woman, and Fitz brought him back to life through the Skill; the dragon Icefyre was freed instead of killed, and dragons returned to the world. Afterwards the Fool, his prophecy fulfilled, went south and out of Fitz's life entirely. Burrich died; Fitz revealed himself to Molly at last and married her, and was granted the holding of Withywoods, where he has lived quietly ever since as Tom Badgerlock. Nettle became Skillmistress at Buckkeep, Dutiful became king, and the persecution of the Witted ended. Far to the south, entirely unknown to any of them, the last dragons were beginning to reclaim an Elderling city on the Rain Wild River.

Fitz and Molly keep Withywoods, a comfortable country holding a long way from Buckkeep, and the life Fitz spent thirty years failing to have is finally the one he is living. Their grown children come and go, Nettle runs the Skill at Buckkeep, and Riddle carries messages between them. During a winter festival a stranger arrives: a pale young woman, hurt and frightened, who has come a very long way looking for FitzChivalry Farseer. Fitz meets her only briefly, and afterwards there is blood where she stood and almost nothing in anyone's memory about her. The incident slides out of his mind as though something has been placed over it, and the message she carried is never delivered.

Molly announces that she is pregnant, which at her age is impossible, and refuses to be talked out of it. The pregnancy runs on past every reasonable term, well over a year and then longer, while Fitz privately agrees with the healers and with Nettle that grief and age have confused her, and hates himself for it. Molly is proved right: she bears a daughter, so tiny that no one expects the child to live through the night, pale and strange-looking and unlike any baby anyone at Withywoods has seen. They name her Bee. Nettle, who has spent years defending her mother, does not know what to make of the sister who has arrived after so long.

Bee grows almost imperceptibly. Years pass in which she remains the size of a much younger child, does not speak, and appears to everyone but her mother to be simple. From inside, she is nothing of the kind: she is alert, retentive and self-possessed, deliberately hiding what she can do because being underestimated is safer. She learns Withywoods' hidden corridors, teaches herself to read, and has vivid, insistent dreams that feel less like sleep than like instructions. Molly is the one person who never doubts her. Fitz is a loving but distracted father who cannot see what is in front of him, and the household treats his daughter as an affliction to be managed politely.

Molly dies, and Withywoods loses the person who held it together and the one person who understood Bee. Fitz's grief is total and largely private, and he handles his small daughter badly at exactly the moment she needs him most. Nettle, made responsible from a distance, wants Bee sent to Buckkeep; Fitz will not allow it. Chade takes the opportunity to solve two of his own problems by lodging them at Withywoods: a young woman called Shun, expensively raised, badly behaved and the target of murder attempts, and FitzVigilant, a disinherited scribe with enemies of his own who is to serve as Bee's tutor. Neither of them is told plainly why Chade is so interested in their safety, and neither is any use to Bee.

The attempts on FitzVigilant's life follow him out of Buckkeep, and a beating leaves him half-broken and Fitz hunting for whoever arranged it. Fitz's old trade comes back to him more easily than he likes. At Withywoods the household reorganizes itself around the two guests: Shun takes rooms, servants and precedence, and treats Bee with an open contempt that nobody corrects, while Fitz is away, preoccupied or simply not looking. Bee, displaced in her own home and mourning her mother, retreats further into her dreams and her secret knowledge of the house, and begins to write down what she sees at night.

FitzVigilant recovers and takes up his duties as tutor, badly at first, and Bee is put into a schoolroom with the estate's children, where she is a curiosity. She finds one genuine ally in Perseverance, a stable boy who treats her as a person rather than an oddity. The household settles into an uneasy peace. Fitz begins, slowly and imperfectly, to see his daughter as she is: not simple, not damaged, but hiding, and formidably capable underneath it. He starts teaching her what he knows, and the two of them build something like a relationship out of lessons, journals and shared silences.

Bee's dreams become undeniable. They are prophetic in the same way the Fool's were, they arrive in sequences she is compelled to record, and some of them show things that have not happened yet to people she has never met. She keeps her journals hidden. Meanwhile the past reaches for Withywoods again: the pale messenger who was lost at the winter festival is remembered in fragments, and the evidence points to something that can take memories out of people's heads, that has been operating in the Six Duchies for years, and that is looking for someone. Chade goes on managing his children from Buckkeep, Nettle and Riddle go on being unable to marry, and Fitz remains a country holder with an assassin's reflexes and no expectation of needing them.

At Buckkeep, a beggar beaten half to death at the gates proves to be the Fool. He is blind, maimed by torture, and terrified, and what he has come to say is that the Servants of Clerres, the order that bred and raised him and that he escaped, took him back and broke him, and that they are hunting a child he calls his unexpected son. He sent messengers north for years and none of them arrived. Fitz hides him and begins healing him with the Skill. At the same moment, Withywoods is raided: pale strangers and Chalcedean soldiers ride in behind a fog that erases memory as it passes, so the people watching forget what they are seeing. Revel is killed defending the door, FitzVigilant is cut down, Perseverance is left for dead, and Bee and Shun are taken away. Almost no one who survives remembers that anything happened at all, and Fitz, hundreds of miles away with the friend he thought he had lost forever, has no idea that his daughter is gone.

characters.description: The bastard son of the long-dead Prince Chivalry, trained in his youth as a royal assassin and carrier of both Farseer magics, the Skill and the despised animal-bond Wit. Believed dead by nearly everyone for fifteen years, he lives quietly in a remote cottage under the name Tom Badgerlock with his wolf and the orphan boy he has raised. He is in his mid-thirties, scarred, still troubled by the damage the Skill and old beatings did him, and determined to stay out of the court's reach.
characters.name: FitzChivalry Farseer

characters.description: The wolf Fitz has been Wit-bonded to since he was a boy, so long joined that the two share thoughts, senses and sometimes bodies. He is old now, stiff in the mornings and slower on a hunt than he will admit, and he watches Fitz with the blunt affection and blunter honesty of a partner who cannot be lied to.
characters.name: Nighteyes

characters.description: The old assassin who trained Fitz in poisons, subtlety and service to the Farseer throne, and who has since become the crown's quietest and most powerful adviser. Vain about his appearance, endlessly persuasive, and still working from concealed rooms and secret stairways, he arrives at Fitz's cottage after years of silence with a request the throne badly needs answered.
characters.name: Chade Fallstar

characters.description: The foundling Fitz took in and raised as his son, now a young man of about fifteen with mismatched eyes and no trade. He is good-natured and eager for a wider life than a hermit's cottage offers, and the question of finding him an apprenticeship, and paying the fee for it, is the practical worry that shapes Fitz's choices.
characters.name: Hap

characters.description: The heir to the Six Duchies throne, son of the dead King-in-Waiting Verity and Queen Kettricken, a boy of about fifteen who has grown up entirely in his mother's shadow and Chade's. He has never been taught the Skill, and a betrothal to an Outislander noblewoman is being arranged to secure peace with the islands.
characters.name: Prince Dutiful

characters.description: The minstrel who travelled with Fitz on his hardest journey and made his deeds into a song, and who has visited his cottage as a lover in the years since. Ambitious, comfortable at court, and impatient with the small life Fitz has chosen, she brings him news of Buckkeep and the wider world on her own terms.
characters.name: Starling Birdsong

characters.description: A travelling hedge-witch who makes charms for luck, sleep, gardens and attraction, and whose small practical magic has nothing to do with the Skill or the Wit. Warm, shrewd and unbothered by other people's secrets, she befriends Fitz on the road and later proves useful to him in Buckkeep Town.
characters.name: Jinna

characters.description: Fitz's oldest friend, once the colourless jester of King Shrewd's court, who named himself the White Prophet and Fitz his Catalyst, the one person whose choices can shift the course of the world. He returns after years abroad transformed in appearance, his skin and eyes now a warm gold, and presents himself in the Six Duchies as Lord Golden, a wealthy and affected Jamaillian noble in need of a servant.
characters.name: The Fool

characters.description: The Mountain-born widow of Verity and reigning Queen of the Six Duchies, ruling as regent for her son. Direct, austere and still an outsider to Buckkeep's court manners, she governs by the Mountain ideal of the ruler as Sacrifice, and she has never stopped grieving the man Fitz served.
characters.name: Queen Kettricken

characters.description: The Queen's Huntswoman, a capable and self-possessed young woman assigned to help search for the missing prince. She knows the country and the great houses, and she has family connections among the Witted that she would rather not discuss.
characters.name: Laurel

characters.description: The young heir of the Bresinga family, whose mother's holding of Galekeep entertained the prince on the hunt from which he disappeared. Grieving his father, awkwardly hospitable, and plainly hiding something about the household's guests and the prince's visit.
characters.name: Civil Bresinga

characters.description: A sleek hunting cat that keeps close company with the prince. To anyone with the Wit the bond between them is obvious and wrong: the animal leads and the boy follows, and the pull it exerts on him is far stronger than an ordinary partnership between beast and man.
characters.name: The Hunting Cat

characters.description: The leader of the Piebalds, a militant faction of Witted who have abandoned the old secrecy. Where most Old Blood folk hide to survive, he intends to force recognition by exposing Witted nobles to their neighbours and by placing a Witted hand on the Farseer throne, and he treats other people's lives as acceptable costs.
characters.name: Laudwine

characters.description: An Old Blood woman, sister to the Piebald leader, who did not accept death when her body failed. Rather than let her spirit disperse she lodged herself in the mind of her bond-animal, and from there she has been working patiently toward a living human body to inhabit.
characters.name: Peladine

recaps.ending: Fitz kills the cat, ending Peladine with it, and the prince is freed of the compulsion that had been eating him. Laudwine escapes badly maimed, still holding the Piebalds' threat to expose Witted nobles, and Fitz and Dutiful bring the party home in time for the betrothal, which goes forward with the Outislander narcheska as planned. During the rescue Fitz and Dutiful were joined mind to mind, so the prince now knows exactly who his mother's new servant is, and Kettricken and Chade formally take Fitz back into the family's service as Dutiful's Skill teacher and the Queen's man. He will live at Buckkeep as Tom Badgerlock, servant to Lord Golden, with a stool in Chade's tower and a boy to teach. Nighteyes, worn out by the journey and by carrying Fitz through the fight, dies quietly, and Fitz is left for the first time in his adult life without the other half of himself. Hap is apprenticed to a woodworker in Buckkeep Town, Starling is gone from his life for good, and the Fool has taken up residence at court in his Lord Golden guise with Fitz at his shoulder. The Piebalds remain at large, the Six Duchies still hang their Witted, and the marriage bargain with the Out Islands is only beginning to be paid for.
recaps.in_short: Fifteen years after the Red Ship war, FitzChivalry Farseer lives as Tom Badgerlock in a remote cottage with his wolf Nighteyes and his foster son Hap, letting the kingdom go on believing him dead. His old mentor Chade wants him back at Buckkeep to teach the Skill to Prince Dutiful, and his old friend the Fool returns in a new guise as the wealthy foreigner Lord Golden. When Dutiful vanishes days before a politically vital betrothal to an Outislander noblewoman, Fitz agrees to find him and takes service with Lord Golden as cover. The search leads through country full of Witted folk to the Piebalds, a militant faction who have deliberately bonded the prince to a hunting cat carrying the spirit of their leader's dead sister, intending to take his body and his throne. Fitz kills the cat, frees Dutiful, and brings him home for the betrothal, and in the process is bound to the boy mind to mind and drawn permanently back into Farseer service. The victory costs him Nighteyes, who dies soon after their return, leaving Fitz alone at Buckkeep as Lord Golden's servant and the prince's secret Skill master.

recaps.text: Previously, in the Farseer trilogy: FitzChivalry Farseer is the acknowledged bastard of Prince Chivalry, heir to the Six Duchies throne, whose existence forced his father to abdicate. Raised in the stables of Buckkeep Castle by the stablemaster Burrich, he was claimed by King Shrewd, trained in secret as a royal assassin by the old poisoner Chade, and taught the Farseer magic called the Skill. He also carried the Wit, the despised bond-magic between human and animal, and joined for life with a wolf, Nighteyes. Through the long Red Ship war he served Chivalry's brother Verity and Verity's Mountain-born queen, Kettricken, and was betrayed by the youngest brother, Regal, who usurped the throne, killed King Shrewd, and had Fitz beaten and left to die in a cell. Fitz survived only by sheltering his mind in the wolf; the kingdom buried him, and so did Molly, the woman he loved, who married Burrich and bore Fitz's daughter Nettle without Fitz ever claiming either of them. Guided by the Fool, the pale court jester who called himself the White Prophet and Fitz his Catalyst, Fitz crossed the kingdom to find Verity, who had spent his life carving a stone dragon. The waking dragons drove the Red Ships from the coast and ended the war. Verity died in the making of his, leaving Kettricken carrying his heir, and Fitz, presumed dead and content to remain so, walked away from the court with his wolf. Far to the south, in Bingtown and the Rain Wilds, dragons were returning to the world by other means entirely, none of which he knows anything about.

Fifteen years on, Fitz lives as Tom Badgerlock in an isolated cottage with Nighteyes and Hap, the foundling he has raised, scratching a living from ink and a garden. Chade appears after years of silence to tell him the Farseer line needs him: Prince Dutiful, Verity and Kettricken's son, has the Skill in him and no one to teach it, and Chade himself has never been able to learn the magic he covets. Fitz refuses. Starling, the minstrel who has been his occasional lover, visits and finds the refusal foolish, and their long, unequal arrangement runs out; Fitz learns how little of her life he was ever part of. On the road he meets Jinna, a travelling hedge-witch, and is reminded that the world has gone on without him. Then the Fool arrives, changed again: his skin and eyes have gone gold, and he is playing the part of Lord Golden, a rich and affected Jamaillian noble touring the Six Duchies. He tells Fitz that he is still the White Prophet, that Fitz is still his Catalyst, and that their work is not finished.

Hap needs an apprenticeship Fitz cannot afford, and Nighteyes is visibly aging; the quiet life is closing. Fitz's old grievances with Chade, with Starling, and with his own choices are aired without being settled. Then the summons Chade always expected to send arrives in earnest: Prince Dutiful has disappeared from Buckkeep only days before a betrothal ceremony that is meant to end generations of hostility with the Out Islands. If the heir cannot be produced, the alliance collapses and the court will learn the Farseer boy has run. Fitz takes the sword Chade sends with the message and agrees to go, on the understanding that this is one task and not a return to service.

Fitz reaches Buckkeep for the first time in fifteen years and is installed as Tom Badgerlock, manservant to Lord Golden, a disguise that lets him move through the castle unremarked. He climbs to Chade's tower rooms, sees Kettricken again, and learns the part of the problem no one will say aloud: the prince is Witted, the beast-magic the Six Duchies still hangs people for, and there are signs he has been drawn away by others of Old Blood. Fitz begins reaching for his own long-neglected Skill and finds it painful and unreliable. Jinna's charms and Buckkeep Town's gossip fill in a little more. With Laurel, the Queen's Huntswoman, and the Fool riding as Lord Golden, Fitz sets out to track Dutiful down quietly before the court notices he is gone.

The trail leads to Galekeep, the Bresinga holding where Dutiful was hunting when he vanished. The family and their young heir Civil are nervously hospitable and clearly complicit in something, and Fitz finds evidence that the household keeps company with the Witted. Laurel admits she has Old Blood kin of her own, and that a faction called the Piebalds has broken with the old rule of hiding: they mean to force the kingdom to accept the Wit, and they punish Witted folk who stay silent. Riding on with the Fool and Nighteyes, Fitz pieces together that the prince was not simply lured away but deliberately caught. Between Fitz and the Fool, old feeling surfaces that neither of them resolves.

Following the trail through inns, standing stones and Wit-signs, Fitz finally reaches Dutiful and finds the boy in company with a hunting cat he is Wit-bonded to and entirely besotted with. The bond is wrong: the animal directs the prince rather than partnering him, and Dutiful, lonely and untaught, has given himself over to it. Fitz makes contact with him mind to mind through the Skill, which links the two of them more deeply than either intended, and tries to talk him into coming home. Dutiful refuses to leave the cat. Meanwhile the Piebalds close in, and it becomes clear the prince was taken for a purpose rather than for ransom.

On the coast the trap closes. The Piebalds, led by Laudwine, have arranged everything: the cat carries the lodged spirit of his dead sister Peladine, an Old Blood woman who refused to die and has been waiting for a human body. Dutiful is being hollowed out so she can wear him, and a Witted Farseer under Piebald control would give them the throne. Fitz, Nighteyes, the Fool and Laurel fight to get the prince clear. Fitz kills the cat, which destroys Peladine with it, and Laudwine escapes with terrible injuries and with his faction's other weapon intact: he can name Witted nobles, including the prince, to a kingdom that hangs them. Dutiful, freed and grieving the animal he loved, agrees to come home.

The party returns to Buckkeep in time for the betrothal, which proceeds with the Outislander narcheska as arranged. Dutiful, bound to Fitz by the Skill contact that saved him, knows who his mother's new servant really is, and Kettricken and Chade take Fitz formally back into Farseer service as the prince's secret Skill master. He will stay at Buckkeep as Tom Badgerlock, servant to Lord Golden, with Hap apprenticed to a woodworker in Buckkeep Town below. Nighteyes, spent by the journey and by carrying Fitz through the fight, dies, and Fitz is left without the companion who has shared his mind since boyhood. The Piebalds are still free and still able to expose the Witted, the Wit is still a hanging matter in the Six Duchies, and the price of the Outislander marriage has not yet been named.

characters.description: The Farseer bastard the Six Duchies believe long dead, living at Buckkeep as the servant Tom Badgerlock, secret Skill master to Prince Dutiful and a member of the coterie Chade has rebuilt. He is bound for the Out Islands on a quest to kill a dragon, carrying a private decision about his oldest friend that he has not told anyone, and a stack of unfinished business: a daughter who does not know him, a woman he gave up, and a name he is not allowed to use.
characters.name: FitzChivalry Farseer

characters.description: The White Prophet, living at Buckkeep in the golden-skinned guise of the foreign noble Lord Golden. He and Fitz are barely speaking after the quarrel that ended their old ease, and he is insistent that he must sail to Aslevjal with the expedition, even though he has admitted that every vision he has of that island ends with his own death.
characters.name: The Fool

characters.description: The old assassin and royal adviser, now also a Skill student and the driving force behind the coterie. He plans the expedition, manages the politics behind it, and is prepared to be ruthless about individual people in the service of the Farseer line, including those he is fond of.
characters.name: Chade Fallstar

characters.description: The heir to the Six Duchies, publicly committed to bringing back the head of the dragon Icefyre as the price of his betrothal to the narcheska. He is growing into his responsibilities faster than he would like, still hiding the Wit that would cost him the throne, and Skill-linked to the servant who guards him.
characters.name: Prince Dutiful

characters.description: Queen of the Six Duchies and regent for her son, holding the kingdom together while its heir sails north on an errand she cannot refuse without losing the Outislander peace. She continues to defend the Witted against her nobles' appetite for hangings.
characters.name: Queen Kettricken

characters.description: The castle drudge whose enormous untrained Skill makes him indispensable to the coterie, taken along on the voyage because the prince's Skill link to home depends on him. He is small, stubborn, fond of sweets and pink sugar cakes, terrified of the sea, and completely unable to keep his misery to himself: what Thick feels, everyone with any Skill feels too.
characters.name: Thick

characters.description: The Outislander girl betrothed to Dutiful, who set the dragon's head as her bride price before the whole Six Duchies court. Proud and brittle in equal measure, she is returning to her own islands with the expedition, and her arrogance keeps slipping to show something much closer to desperation underneath.
characters.name: Narcheska Elliania

characters.description: Elliania's uncle and protector, an Outislander warrior of her mothershouse. He is grimly cooperative with the Six Duchies, unfailingly watchful of his niece, and carrying a burden he will not name to foreigners.
characters.name: Peottre Blackwater

characters.description: The Old Blood Wit-master who came to Buckkeep as the Queen's guest, bonded to a seabird named Risk. Calm, patient and impossible to intimidate, he joins the expedition as the Witted members' teacher and conscience, and he keeps quietly pointing out to Tom Badgerlock the things Tom would rather not look at.
characters.name: Web

characters.description: The runaway boy in Web's charge, a fine archer, Witted, and utterly estranged from the father who tried to beat the magic out of him. He sails with the expedition rather than go home. His father is Burrich, which means Fitz spends the voyage in the company of a boy who is, unknowably to either of them, his own stepson.
characters.name: Swift

characters.description: Fitz's daughter, who has never been told he exists and who knows him only as a wolf in her dreams. She is a powerful natural Skill user, and with the coterie sailing beyond easy reach, Chade means to use her as the link that holds the expedition to Buckkeep whether Fitz consents or not.
characters.name: Nettle

characters.description: The stablemaster who raised Fitz, and the man who has spent the last twenty years as Molly's husband and father to her children, believing Fitz dead. Blunt, upright, hard on his sons about the Wit he regards as a curse, and still the closest thing to a father Fitz ever had.
characters.name: Burrich

characters.description: A pale, colourless woman out of the Red Ship war, who worked through the raider Kebal Rawbread to break the Six Duchies and who was believed destroyed with him. She set herself against the White Prophet's vision of the world and has never stopped, and she has made the frozen island of Aslevjal her own.
characters.name: The Pale Woman

characters.description: A dark-skinned man living alone on Aslevjal, weathered by decades of solitude and unsurprised by the arrival of foreigners. He was a White Prophet in his own time, long before the Fool, and he stayed on the island after his work was done.
characters.name: Prilkop

characters.description: The black dragon of Outislander legend, said to be buried in the glacier of Aslevjal. He is not a carving, a corpse or a story: he is an ancient dragon trapped alive in the ice, aware, furious and utterly indifferent to human purposes.
characters.name: Icefyre

characters.description: A great blue-and-silver queen dragon out of the south, the first true dragon to fly the world in generations, hatched from the last serpent cocoons of the Rain Wilds. She has spent years searching for another of her kind, and she does not negotiate with humans so much as instruct them.
characters.name: Tintaglia

recaps.ending: Icefyre is cut free of the glacier and lives, the Pale Woman's power on Aslevjal is broken and she does not leave the island, and Elliania is released from the coercion that made her demand a dragon's head. The bride price is paid to the letter when Icefyre consents to lay his head on the narcheska's hearth, and the Farseer and Outislander marriage stands. The Fool, killed under torture, is brought back to life by Fitz through the Skill at a cost neither of them fully accounts for, and then leaves: his prophecy is fulfilled, his work in the world is done, and he goes south with Prilkop, telling Fitz goodbye. Fitz returns to the Six Duchies through the Skill-pillars and reaches Burrich as he is dying, in time to be recognized and forgiven. Freed at last from the dead man he was pretending to be, Fitz goes to Molly, tells her the truth, and they marry; the crown grants him the holding of Withywoods, where he lives on as Holder Tom Badgerlock rather than take back the Farseer name he is offered. Nettle learns who her father is and comes to Buckkeep to serve the Skill. Dutiful acknowledges his own Wit, and with Kettricken and Web behind him the persecution of the Witted begins to end. Fitz has the ordinary life he was never supposed to get, and no idea where in the world the Fool has gone.
recaps.in_short: Committed to bringing the narcheska the head of the dragon Icefyre, Prince Dutiful sails for the Out Islands with Chade, Thick, Web, Swift and Fitz. Convinced that the Fool will die on Aslevjal, Fitz conspires to leave him behind, a betrayal the Fool does not forgive. In the islands Fitz learns why Elliania set the price: her mother and sister are hostages of the Pale Woman, the White Prophet's ancient rival, who wants the last dragon of the north dead. On Aslevjal the party finds Prilkop, a White Prophet from an earlier age, and discovers that Icefyre is alive in the ice. The Fool comes anyway, is captured, and is tortured to death in the Pale Woman's tunnels beneath the glacier. Tintaglia arrives and demands the dragon be freed rather than killed; Icefyre is cut loose and the Pale Woman destroyed. Fitz brings the Fool back from death through the Skill, and Icefyre satisfies the vow by laying his head on the narcheska's hearth. The Fool departs for the south with Prilkop. Fitz returns home in time to see Burrich die, then reveals himself to Molly at last and marries her, settling at Withywoods, while Dutiful admits his Wit publicly and Nettle learns who her father is.

recaps.text: Previously: FitzChivalry Farseer, royal bastard, trained assassin, Skill user and Witted, was left for dead in Regal's dungeons during the Red Ship war and let the world go on believing it. Molly, the woman he loved, married the stablemaster Burrich and raised Fitz's daughter Nettle as Burrich's own. Guided by the Fool, the White Prophet who named Fitz his Catalyst, Fitz found Verity, whose stone dragon ended the war; Verity died in the making of it, leaving Queen Kettricken carrying his heir. Fifteen quiet years later, in Fool's Errand, Chade brought Fitz back to court to teach the Skill to Prince Dutiful. The Fool returned transformed, playing the wealthy foreigner Lord Golden, and Fitz became his manservant Tom Badgerlock. Dutiful had been lured away and bonded to a hunting cat carrying a dead Old Blood woman's spirit, part of a Piebald plot to control the throne; Fitz freed him at the cost of his wolf Nighteyes, and stayed on as the prince's secret Skill master. In Golden Fool, Chade rebuilt a Skill coterie around himself, Dutiful, Fitz and Thick, a despised castle drudge with immense untaught talent. Kettricken began ending the persecution of the Witted, bringing the Wit-master Web to court along with Burrich's runaway son Swift. Fitz met his daughter Nettle only in dreams, refusing to be named, and fought Chade's plan to recruit her. A Bingtown woman named Jek greeted Lord Golden as an old friend she had known as a woman called Amber and spoke of the Fool's love for Fitz; Fitz's reaction broke the friendship. At the betrothal ceremony the Outislander narcheska Elliania demanded, as her bride price, the head of the dragon Icefyre, frozen in the glacier of Aslevjal. Dutiful accepted, and the Fool admitted his visions of that island end in his death.

Buckkeep prepares the expedition to Aslevjal. Chade assembles the party around the prince: himself, Thick as the Skill anchor, Web and his pupil Swift, guardsmen, the Witted Civil, and Tom Badgerlock. Burrich comes seeking his runaway son, and Fitz keeps out of his sight rather than face the man who raised him. Chade insists that the coterie will need Nettle to hold the Skill link back to Buckkeep once the fleet is at sea, and Fitz is forced to give ground on the daughter he has protected from all of this. Meanwhile Fitz makes a decision alone: because the Fool foresees his own death on Aslevjal, the Fool will not be permitted to sail. Fitz arranges it quietly, and the ships leave the Fool behind in the Six Duchies, betrayed by the one person he trusted absolutely.

The voyage north is wretched. Thick is violently seasick and, being unable to contain anything, broadcasts his misery through the Skill to everyone sensitive to it, until Fitz spends most of the crossing nursing him. In the Out Islands the expedition meets the Hetgurd, the council of clans, which formally opposes killing Icefyre: the dragon is a god-beast of the islands, and its death would be an offence against every clan. They allow the attempt but send an observer to witness and to condemn. The party is taken to the narcheska's mothershouse, and the customs of the matrilineal Outislander clans make it plain how much of Elliania's standing rests on the women of her line.

At the mothershouse the truth behind the bride price finally surfaces. Elliania never wanted the dragon's head: her mother and her small sister are held hostage by the Pale Woman, the colourless enemy who worked through the raider Kebal Rawbread during the Red Ship war and who was believed dead with him. She survived, she has made Aslevjal hers, and she wants the last dragon of the north destroyed. Elliania has been made her instrument, and Peottre has been shielding a child forced to play politics with knives at her family's throats. The expedition sails on to Aslevjal knowing it is walking into a trap laid for it years in advance.

Aslevjal is a glacier over a buried Elderling city. The party finds a solitary dark-skinned inhabitant, Prilkop, who turns out to be a White Prophet of an earlier age, left behind when his own work was finished. Digging into the ice, they discover that Icefyre is no legend and no carcass: he is alive, ancient, enraged and aware, and freeing him or killing him are equally dangerous propositions. The camp fractures over what to do, the Hetgurd's observer records everything, and Fitz learns that the Fool did not stay behind after all. He followed the expedition north on his own, and somewhere on the island he has fallen into the Pale Woman's hands.

Beneath the glacier lies the Pale Woman's realm: tunnels and Elderling corridors, her forged and broken servants, and a mind that has spent decades preparing for this. Thick sickens badly and the coterie's Skill work becomes both essential and dangerous, with Nettle holding the far end of the link from Buckkeep. Fitz goes down under the ice after the Fool, and the search costs the party dearly in people and in nerve. The Pale Woman is not interested in ransom or bargaining: she means to end the Fool's line of prophecy for good, and she has had him long enough to do it.

Fitz reaches the Fool too late. The Pale Woman has tortured him to death, and Fitz carries the body out of her tunnels. At the same time the argument over Icefyre is settled from outside: Tintaglia, the great blue queen dragon out of the southern Rain Wilds, comes to Aslevjal. She has searched the world for another of her kind and she will not permit the last male dragon to be killed by humans. Her command reverses the whole purpose of the expedition. The Six Duchies party, the Outislanders and the Hetgurd's witness must now free the dragon they came to behead, and dig him out of ice that has held him for generations.

Icefyre is cut free and lives. The Pale Woman's hold on the island is broken and she does not survive it, and the hostages she used to force Elliania's hand are accounted for. Refusing to accept the Fool's death, Fitz uses the Skill, Prilkop's guidance and the memory-stone of the buried city to draw his friend back from death, restoring him to his own body whole. The White Prophet's prophecy is complete: dragons are in the world again, which is what the Fool's entire life was bent toward. The expedition begins the long business of getting home, and Elliania, freed of the compulsion that shaped her demand, is a different person to the girl who made it.

The vow is satisfied on its own terms when Icefyre agrees to lay his head on the narcheska's hearth, giving Dutiful his bride price without a killing, and the Farseer and Outislander alliance holds. Fitz travels home through the Skill-pillars and arrives to find Burrich dying of injuries. He goes to him, is recognized, and the two of them settle twenty years of silence before Burrich dies. Molly is widowed, Burrich's sons are fatherless, and Fitz, who has spent his adult life being officially dead, is finally free to be someone. The Fool, alive and restored, has finished what he came into the world to do, and begins saying his goodbyes.

Fitz goes to Molly, tells her who he is and always was, and they marry; the crown grants him Withywoods, where he settles as Holder Tom Badgerlock, declining the offer to take the Farseer name publicly. Nettle is told the truth about her father and comes to Buckkeep to serve the Skill. Dutiful acknowledges his own Wit, and with Kettricken and Web behind him the hangings and quarterings of the Witted begin to end; Swift and the Old Blood have a place at court. Chade goes on being Chade. The Fool leaves for the south with Prilkop, his prophecy fulfilled and his part in the world's story finished, and Fitz is left with the ordinary life he never expected to have and no way of knowing where his friend has gone.

characters.description: The Farseer bastard, middle-aged holder of Withywoods and lifelong secret of the crown, at Buckkeep for Winterfest under yet another false name while he hides a dying friend in a forgotten room. He is a trained assassin who has not needed to be one for twenty years, a Skill user of formidable and badly disciplined strength, and a father who has spent most of his daughter's life not paying attention.
characters.name: FitzChivalry Farseer

characters.description: The White Prophet, returned to the Six Duchies as a blind, crippled beggar after years in the hands of the order that raised him. His hands and body are ruined, he starts at every sound, and the person underneath is only intermittently the friend Fitz remembers. He has come north with a warning and a demand for vengeance.
characters.name: The Fool

characters.description: The old assassin and king's adviser, very old now, still keeping secret rooms, secret stores and secret children, and still certain that he knows better than anyone what should be done. His appetite for the Skill has never been matched by his talent for it.
characters.name: Chade Fallstar

characters.description: Fitz's eldest daughter, Skillmistress of Buckkeep and the most powerful Skill user in the Six Duchies. She carries the responsibility for the whole coterie, for her father's habit of doing dangerous things without telling anyone, and for a private matter of her own that the court will not approve of.
characters.name: Nettle

characters.description: A guardsman and crown agent, Fitz's closest friend among the living and the man Nettle loves, kept from marrying her by the difference in their rank.
characters.name: Riddle

characters.description: King of the Six Duchies, Verity's son, raised in part by Fitz and fully aware of what his kingdom owes a man it has never been allowed to name.
characters.name: King Dutiful

characters.description: Chade's apprentice, a quick, self-contained young servant trained in the crown's quieter arts and used to being underestimated by everyone in the castle.
characters.name: Ash

characters.description: Fitz and Molly's younger daughter, about nine years old and the size of a much smaller child, taken from her home by strangers who knew exactly what they had come for. She is fiercely observant, keeps her own written record of everything, and dreams true.
characters.name: Bee

characters.description: The pale, soft-spoken leader of the raiders, a woman of the Servants of Clerres who has spent her whole life inside their prophecies and believes she is fulfilling one. She is unfailingly gentle in manner and absolutely without mercy in practice.
characters.name: Dwalia

characters.description: A Chalcedean commander hired to provide the raiders with soldiers, an exiled officer with nothing left to lose and no interest in his employers' religion. He takes his payment in whatever he can seize.
characters.name: Ellik

characters.description: The young woman Chade lodged at Withywoods for her own safety, taken in the raid along with Bee and thrown into a captivity nobody prepared her for. Spoiled, frightened and much tougher than she looks.
characters.name: Shun

characters.description: A crow with white feathers among the black, mobbed by her own kind for it, who attaches herself to Fitz's household. She talks, she remembers, and she is a better spy than most people.
characters.name: Motley

characters.description: The disinherited scribe sent to Withywoods as its tutor, cut down defending the house and left to survive both his wounds and the knowledge that he failed the children in his charge.
characters.name: FitzVigilant

characters.description: The stable boy who was Bee's only real friend at Withywoods, left for dead in the raid and one of the very few people who remembers it clearly. He knows what he saw and he intends to go after her.
characters.name: Perseverance

characters.description: A pale, doughy young Servant travelling with the raiders, whose gift is a fog he can push into people's minds so that they forget what they are looking at and believe whatever he wishes. He is desperate to be loved by the woman who owns him.
characters.name: Vindeliar

characters.description: An Elderling of the Rain Wilds, once a Bingtown Trader's daughter, now effectively the queen of a rediscovered dragon city and one of the shrewdest negotiators in the south.
characters.name: Malta Khuprus

recaps.ending: Fitz destroys the raiders' camp and recovers Shine, but Dwalia takes Bee into a Skill-pillar moments ahead of him, and everything Fitz can find afterwards convinces him that his daughter died in the snow. He comes home to a kingdom that finally names him: Dutiful, Kettricken and Nettle present him to the court as FitzChivalry Farseer, prince of the realm, twenty years after they buried him. Nettle and Riddle are married and expecting a child, Shine and FitzVigilant learn whose children they are, and Chade, aged and damaged, is no longer the man who ran the Six Duchies from behind its walls. None of it touches Fitz. He and the Fool set out south for Clerres to destroy the Servants and everyone in them, taking FitzVigilant, Chade's apprentice and Perseverance with them, travelling as a merchant party. What neither of them knows is that Bee is alive. Carried through the Skill-pillars by Dwalia and lost inside them for months, she emerges at Kelsingra, half-starved and barely conscious, into an Elderling city full of dragons, where Malta Khuprus and the Elderlings take her in and begin working out who she is. She is thousands of miles from home and no one who loves her knows she exists, while her father sails away to avenge a death that never happened.
recaps.in_short: At Buckkeep for Winterfest, Fitz hides the tortured, blinded Fool in a secret room and hears his story: the Servants of Clerres, the order that bred and broke him, are hunting an unexpected son of prophecy. Fitz heals him with the Skill and with Silver taken from Chade's hidden store, silvering his own hand in the process. Then word reaches him of the raid on Withywoods. He Skill-travels home to find his steward dead, his tutor cut down, his people's memories eaten away by a fog, and Bee and Shun gone. Bee, meanwhile, is being carried south by Dwalia's Servants, who believe she is the Shaysim of their prophecies, with the fog-maker Vindeliar bending everyone around them and the Chalcedean mercenary Ellik taking his pay out of Shine. Fitz hunts them across the Six Duchies through the Skill-pillars, tearing himself apart to do it, and finally destroys their camp; he recovers Shine and kills Ellik, but Dwalia escapes into a pillar with Bee, and Fitz is left certain that his daughter is dead. He is publicly acknowledged as Prince FitzChivalry Farseer, then sails south to annihilate Clerres. Bee, lost in the pillars for months, emerges alive at Kelsingra among the Elderlings and their dragons.
